To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the net anion transport system is a conductive process, is inhibited by anion exchange inhibitors, is anion selective, and is not a simple function of the exchange transport system.

the conductive and exchange anion permeabilities of the human red blood cells membrane are not identical, that both processes are inhibited by disulfonic stilbenic inhibitors, and that the conductive anion permeability is anion selective, with the permeability sequence being OH- greater than Cl- greater than HCO3- greater than SO42-.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the anion transport system of the red cell membrane.
the study of the mechanism of anion transport in human red blood cell membranes.
the mechanism by which the human red cell membrane maintains its volume, and the mechanism by which anions cross the cell membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the conductive and exchange anion permeabilities of the human red blood cells are different, but that the conductive permeability is probably a function of the same membrane component as the exchange permeability.

the net anion flux is a combination of the anion exchange process and a DIDS-sensitive process with a different anion selectivity and that the latter may be the same process that has been proposed as the basis for the anion exchange mechanism.
the anion exchange system of human red blood cell membranes is also involved in net anion transport, but that net transport can also occur via a DIDS-insensitive process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DIDS inhibits net anion transport by blocking anion exchange.
the anion exchanger is the principal pathway for anion conductance in the red cell.
the conductive and exchange anion permeabilities are similar in that they are both inhibited by DIDS and are both anion selective, but differ in their selectivity and sensitivity to DIDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are two types of anion transport across the RBC membrane: (1) anion exchange, which occurs via the band 3 protein, and (2) net anion transport, which may occur through the same band 3 protein or a separate protein.
the net anion conductance and the anion exchange conductance are not the same.
the anion transporters in the red blood cell membrane are very sensitive to DIDS, which is a very useful tool for investigating the anion transport process.
